title: Heuristic headroom misprediction causing burst enforcement errors
creator: Priya Raman
description: Summary: Several customers reported sudden throttles and coldstarts during mixed interactive and batch traffic windows despite available reserved pool capacity. Initial triage shows the autoscaler headroom heuristic is underpredicting required live slots for tenants with high short-request frequency and KV-cache occupancy, which causes the burst enforcement subsystem to trigger aggressive throttles and deny burst allocations.
root_cause: The headroom estimator uses an exponentially-weighted metric aggregated at tenant-level which weights request count but does not sufficiently account for per-request token-cost and live-KV cache residency. When traffic mixes many short, low-token requests with occasional long-generation bursts, the estimator under-sizes headroom leading the allocator to view headroom as exhausted and the burst controller to enforce limits even though physical GPU capacity exists. Additionally, a ledger rounding bug in burst-credit accounting caused minor underreporting of available burst credits for affected tenants.
impact: Multiple mid-market customers experienced increased 503s and token latency spikes during weekday morning traffic peaks. Two customers opened escalations; one reported backing-off internal request retry loops which amplified load. Estimated revenue-sensitive tenants impacted: 3 customers with burst SLAs. Overall SLA degradation window ~90 minutes for top-affected tenants.
mitigation_actions: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Emergency mitigation: deployed temporary relaxation to burst-enforcement threshold (allow +20% soft headroom) for VIP tenants to reduce immediate 503s.
2026-03-10 11:15 - Increased reserved pool headroom by adding 2 hot instances into regional pool as short-term capacity buffer.
2026-03-11 02:00 - Backported hotfix to ledger rounding (PR #12847) to stop credit undercount; observed recovered credit balances for impacted tenants.
2026-03-11 06:30 - Customer comms drafted and sent to impacted customers with mitigation summary and ETA for permanent fix.
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Update headroom estimator to weight by expected token-cost and KV-cache residency (token-seconds heuristic). 2) Add per-tenant traffic profile classifier to surface 'short-request-heavy' tenants and use adjusted safety margins for them. 3) Patch burst-credit ledger rounding and add unit/integration tests. 4) Add new telemetry: headroom_estimate_token_seconds, allocator_recommendation, burst_enforce_reason_code and dashboard. 5) Run controlled load tests (mixed workloads) and canary rollout to one region before global deploy.
acceptance_criteria: Headroom estimator correctly predicts required live slots within 10% during synthetic mixed-workload tests (interactive:batch ratios 80:20, 50:50, 20:80).
No customer-facing 503 spikes in canary region for 72 hours after deploy during simulated traffic ramp.
Burst-credit ledger accounts reconcile to exact cents-of-credit (no rounding slip) across 1M credit operations in regression test.
New telemetry surfaces root-cause signals and reduces time-to-detect for similar incidents by >50% (measured in playbook drills).
steps_taken: Reproduced symptom in staging by replaying production traces with mixed short/long requests; observed estimator underprediction.
Runbook created: runbooks/allocator-headroom-misestimate.md (internal DR plan) and linked in ticket.
Implemented and deployed ledger rounding fix (hotfix PR #12847) to prod; validated with reconciliation job.
Implemented prototype token-seconds estimator in a feature branch and performed local load experiments showing improved predictions.
Scheduled full load test (mixed traffic) in staging for 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC.
rollback_plan: If new estimator causes allocation thrash or increased latency: 1) Revert estimator flag to previous algorithm via feature-flag. 2) Re-apply relaxed burst-enforcement as temporary buffer and add 2 hot instances to pool. 3) Notify customers and engage SRE for on-call capacity adjustments.
